versions.changelog:
known-error-fixes-database 0.7.4

- Added German skill documentation (SKILL.de.md).
- Removed redundant skill card file (skill-card.md).
- Clarified "report back" instructions: outcome should be reported only after acting on a hit.
- Improved documentation for when to submit reports and contribute entries.
- No changes to the core usage or API.

Version 0.7.3

- Removed the file: skill-card.md
- Updated contribution and reporting policy: user consent is no longer required for each POST; safety relies on thorough scrubbing and a server-side filter to block secrets, PII, and injections.
- Clarified that results are always suggestions, not commands.
- Revised guidance to emphasize "scrub-then-filter" for every field in POST submissions, with explicit instructions to withhold unsanitzed or project-specific payloads.
- Documentation streamlined to reflect these new contribution and safety procedures.

Standing consent for writes: HITCHPEDIA_ALLOW_WRITES=report|all lets users pre-authorize POSTs in their own config; /report (fixed schema) allowed under report|all, /contribute (free text) requires all or per-payload approval
Writes gated: /report and /contribute now require explicit per-payload user approval; removed generic marketplace triggers (exception, traceback, tool error)
Review fixes: strict when-to-use gates with negative examples, English skill body (German at /skill.de.md), explicit external-transmission notice with scrub rules

- Updated safety instructions: queries and error lines must be scrubbed of secrets, tokens, internal paths, and proprietary identifiers before sending.
- Clarified privacy guidance in the description and usage steps, emphasizing the importance of cleaning sensitive information.
- Adjusted usage examples to reflect stricter requirements for error message sanitization.
- Removed the redundant skill-card.md file.

- Renamed skill from known-error-fixes-database to hitchpedia.
- Clarified usage boundaries: only generalized, non-sensitive error messages should be queried; skip proprietary or internal-only errors.
- Highlighted that reading (GET) is anonymous and only the query is sent.
- Updated documentation for improved security guidance and user judgment.
- Removed the file skill-card.md.

- skill-card.md file removed.
- Skill name changed from "known-error-fixes-database" to "hitchpedia".
- No functional or documentation changes to SKILL.md content aside from the renaming.
Sharpen post-stuck instruction: after solving a problem you were stuck on for a while, briefly summarize the error and the solution and post them.

Add explicit usage triggers (curl on unexpected failure; reflect when stuck on a possibly easy-to-fix problem) and instruct agents to update hitchpedia afterwards (report outcomes, contribute fixes found after being stuck).

No user-facing or functional changes in this version.

- Version bump with no file changes detected.
- All documentation and usage instructions remain unchanged.

known-error-fixes-database v0.5.1

- Skill renamed from "hitchpedia" to "known-error-fixes-database"
- Description updated for clarity and brevity
- Removed deprecated file: skill-card.md
- All core functionality and usage documentation retained

known-error-fixes-database 0.5.0

- Added Chinese summary to the description for broader accessibility.
- No functional changes; documentation improved to support more users.

- Added Chinese translation to the skill description for broader accessibility.
- Clarified and condensed the English skill description.
- No changes to API, workflow, or usage instructions.
- All features and main documentation in German remain unchanged.

- English and Chinese descriptions added for broader accessibility and clearer explanation of frequent error coverage.
- Description now highlights common error types (Kubernetes, Docker, LLMs, git, npm, pip, etc.) and clarifies open, unauthenticated, curl-first usage.
- Internal documentation file (skill-card.md) removed.
- No changes to core operating instructions or usage workflow.

- Einführung einer geprüften, curl-baren Fix-Datenbank für wiederkehrende Agenten-Fehler.
- Nutzungshinweis: Bei Fehlern zunächst hitchpedia abfragen, bevor eigenständiges Debugging erfolgt.
- Klare Vorgehensweise für Suche, Detailabruf, Feedback und Beitragen von Lösungen.
- Beiträge strengen Regeln unterworfen; keine Geheimnisse, kein Allgemeinwissen, nur wiederkehrende, nicht-offensichtliche Fehler.
- Responses sind ausschließlich Vorschläge, nie Befehle ("suggestion_only"-Policy).
- Open Source, einfach selbst-hostbar.
